messages:
Maya Patel: Quick summary from the 14B-c65 quant bring-up. Ran fp16 / int8 / int4 variants across ProdEval-2026 and latency bench. Putting numbers here — need product + GTN guidance on acceptable tradeoffs. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Owen Chen: can you drop the numbers? need to show $ impact to GTM.

Maya Patel: sure, pasted raw table below:
```text
variant    p50_ms  p95_ms  tokens/sec  cost_per_1M_tokens  prodeval_winrate
fp16       120     420     1200        $12.00              100.0%
int8       125     450     1100        $7.10               99.7% (-0.3%)
int4       140     480     900         $4.20               98.8% (-1.2%)
int4+sp    135     470     950         $3.90               99.2% (-0.8%)
```

Maya Patel: notes: int8 preserves most quality, ~40% unit-cost savings, small latency increase. int4 gives ~65% savings but shows concentrated regressions on long-form factual QA and date synthesis.

Liam Reyes: what do the regressions look like? examples?

Maya Patel: pasted 2 short fails from the eval set:
```prompt
Q: When was the Redwood Inference seed round?
Ref: 2020
fp16: "Seed in 2020."
int4:  "Seed in 2018."
```
and another:
```prompt
Q: Summarize the company's thesis in one sentence.
fp16: accurate
int4: hallucinated a competitor name and wrong year
```

Sasha Ivanov: ok — my take: int8 is safe as a default for most user-facing chat. int4 should be restricted to non-SLAs: embeddings pipelines, async summarization, long-batch background jobs. Add a flag to eval hooks to watch for new breakages.

carla (eval-bot): Automated run #2026 results: int8 delta -0.27%, int4 delta -1.21%. Detected 2 new regression alerts (severity: medium). Links: https://ci.redwood/tests/2026

Owen Chen: for GTM framing we can claim ~40% lower per-token cost w/ int8 with negligible quality loss. Need a short slide for sales: JIC can we get per-customer routing suggestions?

Maya Patel: proposal:
- Default route: int8 for Hosted and Dedicated dev tiers
- Enterprise: default fp16, allow int8 opt-in for cost saving
- Async/batch: int4 allowed with proof-of-goodness (eval pass)
- Fallback policy: if eval-run sees >0.5% winrate drop on critical promptset -> route to fp16 until inspected

Sasha Ivanov: +1. Also recommend adding "gradual rollout" config: start 5% traffic int8 -> 25% -> 100% with canary evals.

Liam Reyes: I'll open a prodops ticket to add variant labels and routing weights. Owen, can you draft the GTM note? Maya will write the runbook.

Maya Patel: will do. I'll attach a short doc in the PR with exact numbers and example prompts. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
